title: What is the effect of alarmist media and radiofrequency electromagnetic field (RF‐EMF) exposure on salivary cortisol and non‐specific symptoms?
authors: Verrender Adam; Wallace Nikkeah K.; Loughran Sarah P.; Wallace Chloe; Beange James; Croft Rodney J.
integrity_status: Exact held source PDF/native identity matched; selected passages freshly inspected; no scientific, numerical or human approval asserted
scope: Healthy predominantly young volunteers received an alarmist or control video with known RF-on or RF-off laboratory conditions; immediate symptom ratings and salivary cortisol, not clinical disease.
limitations: Open-label contrast, immediate outcomes and predominantly young healthy volunteers do not establish a biological RF mechanism or clinical syndrome. Cortisol timing and small-effect uncertainty remain; scientific, numerical and human review pending.
citation: Verrender Adam; Wallace Nikkeah K.; Loughran Sarah P.; Wallace Chloe; Beange James; Croft Rodney J.. What is the effect of alarmist media and radiofrequency electromagnetic field (RF‐EMF) exposure on salivary cortisol and non‐specific symptoms? 2025. DOI: 10.1111/aphw.70044.

claims.text: Symptoms increased under openly known exposure compared with known non-exposure. The alarmist-video manipulation increased perceived risk but did not significantly change the symptom or cortisol outcomes in the reported factorial comparisons.
claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 12 to 16, Results and Discussion

claims.text: Because actual exposure and knowledge were bundled in the open condition, the study cannot isolate a pure RF effect. Cortisol timing, anticipatory stress, limited sensitivity to small effects and the nonclinical sample constrain interpretation.
claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 15 to 17, Discussion and limitations

title: Exposure Perception and Symptom Reporting in Idiopathic Environmental Intolerance Attributed to Electromagnetic Fields Using a Co‐Designed Provocation Test
authors: Ledent Maryse; Bordarie Jimmy; Vatovez Benjamin; Dieudonné Maël; Prignot Nicolas; Vanderstraeten Jacques; Bouland Catherine; De Clercq Eva M.
integrity_status: Exact held source PDF/native identity matched; selected passages freshly inspected; no scientific, numerical or human approval asserted
scope: Co-designed individualized real-versus-sham sessions with selected people attributing symptoms to mixed RF and low-frequency sources; acute perception and symptom reports.
limitations: Selected volunteers able to tolerate an individualized protocol, mixed signals and repeated sessions are not a population test of every source or chronic condition. No universal safety or symptom-unreality inference. Scientific, numerical and human review pending.
citation: Ledent Maryse; Bordarie Jimmy; Vatovez Benjamin; Dieudonné Maël; Prignot Nicolas; Vanderstraeten Jacques; Bouland Catherine; De Clercq Eva M.. Exposure Perception and Symptom Reporting in Idiopathic Environmental Intolerance Attributed to Electromagnetic Fields Using a Co‐Designed Provocation Test 2025. DOI: 10.1002/bem.70006.

claims.text: The study did not demonstrate consistent exposure detection or exposure-related symptoms at the collective level. A nominal individual detection finding did not persist when the least-certain session was removed, so that exception should not be treated as robust detection.
claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 14 to 16, individual and collective interpretation

claims.text: Perceived exposure was associated with symptom reporting, but these joint self-reports do not prove a clinical nocebo mechanism. Small selected series, heterogeneous individualized protocols and multiple comparisons limit generalization beyond the tested sessions.
claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 15 to 17, Discussion and limitations

title: Impact of mobile phone-specific electromagnetic fields on DNA damage caused by occupationally relevant exposures: results of ex vivo experiments with peripheral blood mononuclear cells from different demographic groups
authors: Mišík Miroslav; Kundi Michael; Worel Nadine; Ferk Franziska; Hutter Hans-Peter; Grusch Michael; Nersesyan Armen; Herrera Morales Denise; Knasmueller Siegfried
integrity_status: Exact held source PDF/native identity matched; selected passages freshly inspected; no scientific, numerical or human approval asserted
scope: Pooled peripheral blood mononuclear cells from demographic groups, exposed outside the body to a specified mobile-phone-like signal and selected chemical treatments.
limitations: Human-derived pooled cells are not exposed intact people; comet-assay differences are not cancer incidence. Donor variation is hidden by pooling, independent replication is limited and numerical reuse remains held. Scientific, numerical and human review pending.
citation: Mišík Miroslav; Kundi Michael; Worel Nadine; Ferk Franziska; Hutter Hans-Peter; Grusch Michael; Nersesyan Armen; Herrera Morales Denise; Knasmueller Siegfried. Impact of mobile phone-specific electromagnetic fields on DNA damage caused by occupationally relevant exposures: results of ex vivo experiments with peripheral blood mononuclear cells from different demographic groups 2023. DOI: 10.1093/mutage/gead022.

claims.text: The highest tested RF condition increased comet-assay signal in the older normal-weight pooled cells, while lower conditions and younger groups did not show that pattern. The tested combined treatments generally did not enhance chemically induced damage; selected decreases are not evidence of clinical protection.
claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 5 to 9, Results, combined-treatment tables and Discussion

claims.text: Pooled cells and sparse independent experiments cannot describe individual donor susceptibility or cancer risk. Differences in demographic composition, culture conditions and technical replicate wording constrain interpretation of this laboratory DNA-damage endpoint.
claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 2 to 4, Methods; pages 8 to 9, Discussion

title: Autonomous nervous system responses to environmental‐level exposure to 5G's first deployed band (3.5 GHz) in healthy human volunteers
authors: Jamal Layla; Michelant Lisa; Delanaud Stéphane; Hugueville Laurent; Mazet Paul; Lévêque Philippe; Baz Tamara; Bach Véronique; Selmaoui Brahim
integrity_status: Exact held source PDF/native identity matched; selected passages freshly inspected; no scientific, numerical or human approval asserted
scope: Brief controlled far-field exposure in healthy young adults, measuring skin temperature and electrodermal responses to auditory stimuli rather than clinical health or cognition.
limitations: Original-version skin and electrodermal findings are not measured cognition, clinical benefit or long-term disease. Direction/label reconciliation and numerical appraisal remain outstanding; scientific and human review pending.
citation: Jamal Layla; Michelant Lisa; Delanaud Stéphane; Hugueville Laurent; Mazet Paul; Lévêque Philippe; Baz Tamara; Bach Véronique; Selmaoui Brahim. Autonomous nervous system responses to environmental‐level exposure to 5G's first deployed band (3.5 GHz) in healthy human volunteers 2024. DOI: 10.1113/EP092083.

claims.text: Selected regional skin-temperature and electrodermal measures differed across the tested conditions, while not every measure showed an exposure-related finding. These physiological responses do not themselves establish cognitive improvement, injury or disease.
claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 6 to 11, Results, Figures and Discussion

claims.text: The authors restrict interpretation to the tested short-term conditions and call for confirmation. Small selected samples, related repeated measurements and unresolved direction or labeling questions require restraint; no numerical or uniform-direction electrodermal summary is released.
claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 10 to 11, Discussion and Conclusion

title: 1.7 GHz long-term evolution radiofrequency electromagnetic field with stable power monitoring and efficient thermal control has no effect on the proliferation of various human cell types
authors: Goh Jaeseong; Suh Dongwha; Park Gyuyeon; Jeon Sangbong; Lee Youngseung; Kim Nam; Song Kiwon
integrity_status: Exact held source PDF/native identity matched; selected passages freshly inspected; no scientific, numerical or human approval asserted
scope: Cultured cell models under a specified LTE signal with feedback power monitoring and temperature control, including a separate cooling-disabled comparison.
limitations: Specific cell models, apparatus and selected endpoints do not measure human disease or lifetime exposure. Replicate wording and the limited independent experiments constrain inference; numerical release, scientific appraisal and human review remain pending.
citation: Goh Jaeseong; Suh Dongwha; Park Gyuyeon; Jeon Sangbong; Lee Youngseung; Kim Nam; Song Kiwon. 1.7 GHz long-term evolution radiofrequency electromagnetic field with stable power monitoring and efficient thermal control has no effect on the proliferation of various human cell types 2024. DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0302936.

claims.text: With thermal and power control, the measured proliferation and selected cell-cycle, stress or DNA-damage assays did not show a significant RF-related pattern. Disabling cooling changed temperature and growth-related measurements, emphasizing the importance of exposure-system control.
claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 6 to 11, Results, Figures and Discussion

claims.text: A cooling-disabled comparison changes thermal conditions together with the exposure setup and does not establish a universal explanation for every prior study. Limited independent replication and nonsignificant cellular comparisons are not proof of equivalence, human safety or absence of all tissue-specific effects.
claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 8 to 11, Discussion and experimental limitations
